Cadra Platform Documentation

Cadra Platform API

The Cadra Platform API is the canonical interface to the Cadra system of record for asset, facility, and service lifecycle management.

This specification describes the version 1 (v1) API. The API surface is organised around three core domains — locations, assets, and service requests — plus an integration fabric (connectors, webhooks, ingestion services, identity, and platform administration).

Audience

This specification is for:

  • Application developers building tenant-side applications that integrate with Cadra (dashboards, workflow tools, mobile applications)
  • Integration engineers building connectors between Cadra and external systems (ERPs, identity providers, document management)
  • Operations engineers integrating Cadra with monitoring, alerting, and management systems

Status and roadmap

Endpoints in this specification are marked with availability status:

  • Available — implemented and operational in the current Cadra release
  • 90-day roadmap — committed for delivery within the next 90 days
  • 180-day roadmap — committed for delivery within the next 180 days
  • Directional — on the longer-term roadmap without committed dates

Partners should design integrations against the Available surface first; roadmap endpoints can be planned for but should not be relied upon for committed delivery dates outside the explicit roadmap horizons.

Versioning

This API is versioned by URL prefix: /api/v1/.... Version 1 is the only currently published version. Breaking changes to v1 will not be made; new capabilities are added as new endpoints or new optional parameters. Significant breaking changes would result in a new version (v2) with both versions running in parallel for a transition period of at least 12 months.

Authentication

The API supports four authentication mechanisms:

  1. OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials — for machine-to-machine integration (the most common pattern for partner integrations)
  2. OpenID Connect (OIDC) Authorization Code Flow — for human-user authentication via federated identity providers
  3. Personal Access Tokens — for individual user API access outside the UI
  4. Mutual TLS — for high-security machine-to-machine integration (Sovereign edition deployments)

All requests must include an Authorization header with a valid Bearer token (or use mTLS where configured). Unauthenticated requests receive a 401 response.

See the Authentication section for detailed flows.

Multi-tenancy

Cadra is multi-tenant. Every authenticated principal belongs to exactly one tenant; the API enforces tenant scope at every layer. There is no cross-tenant access; an authenticated token from tenant A cannot read or modify tenant B's data through any API path.

Tenant identification is implicit in the authentication token's tenant claim. Clients do not pass tenant identifiers explicitly in requests.

Rate limiting

Rate limits are enforced per tenant, per credential, per endpoint class. Default limits vary by edition; specific limits are communicated to tenants during onboarding.

Every response includes rate limit headers:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit — the limit for this credential/endpoint class
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining — remaining quota
  • X-RateLimit-Reset — Unix timestamp when the quota resets

When limits are exceeded, the API returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header.

Idempotency

POST endpoints that create resources accept an optional Idempotency-Key header. Repeated requests with the same idempotency key (within a 24-hour window) return the original response without creating duplicate resources. Recommended for any creation operation; required for any creation operation in untrusted network conditions.

Pagination

List endpoints use cursor-based pagination. The response includes a cursor field; pass this as the cursor query parameter to fetch the next page. Page size is controlled via the limit parameter (default 50, maximum 200).

Errors

Error responses use a structured format:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "location_not_found",
    "message": "Location with id 'loc_01HXY...' not found",
    "details": {}
  },
  "request_id": "req_01HXY..."
}

The code field is a stable, machine-readable error identifier. The message field is a human-readable description. The details field may contain additional structured information specific to the error.

The request_id field appears in all responses (success and error) and is the correlation identifier for support enquiries.

Events and webhooks

Cadra emits events when significant operational state changes occur. External systems can subscribe to webhook delivery of these events to receive near-real-time notifications without polling.

The webhook event catalogue is documented in the Webhooks section.

Conventions

  • British English in field descriptions
  • UUID identifiers for entities (formatted as 26-character ULID-style strings)
  • ISO 8601 timestamps in UTC (e.g. 2026-05-20T14:32:18.451Z)
  • ISO 4217 currency codes
  • GeoJSON for geographic coordinates
  • Plural nouns in resource paths (/locations, /assets)
  • Kebab-case for multi-word resource paths (/api/v1/request-types)

Locations

Operations on the locations domain — the hierarchical map of where the tenant operates.

Locations have type (campus, building, floor, room, etc.), hierarchy (parent-child), lifecycle state, geographic coordinates, and characteristics. The locations register is the foundation of the Cadra data model — assets exist at locations, service requests happen at locations.

See PRD section 7 for the full domain specification.

List locations

Returns a paginated list of locations. Supports filtering by type, lifecycle state, parent, custodian, and tags.

For free-text search or geographic queries, use POST /locations/search.

OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken

lifecycle_state
Array of strings (LocationLifecycleState)
Items Enum: "planned" "active" "under_renovation" "decommissioned" "archived"
Example: lifecycle_state=active
parent_id

custodian_id

Array of strings

Create location

Creates a new location. The parent location, if specified, must exist and be in active or under_renovation state.

Locations are created in planned state by default; transition to active separately via /locations/{id}/transition.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
header Parameters
Idempotency-Key
string

Optional idempotency key. Repeated requests with the same key within 24 hours return the original response.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
code
required
string <= 64 characters
name
required
string <= 255 characters
description
string <= 2000 characters
type
required
string (LocationType)
Enum: "campus" "building" "floor" "wing_or_zone" "room" "outdoor_area" "field_office" "vehicle_base" "external_location"

The type of location. Each tenant may extend this set with custom types.

  • campus — A complex of related buildings on contiguous land
  • building — A discrete structure with its own address
  • floor — A horizontal slice of a building
  • wing_or_zone — A sub-area of a floor
  • room — A discrete enclosed space
  • outdoor_area — A defined open space (parking, generator yard, grounds)
  • field_office — A remote operational location
  • vehicle_base — The home location of mobile assets
  • external_location — An off-premises place the organisation operates in
parent_id
string or null
object (Address)
object (GeoPoint)
custodian_id
string or null
object
tags
Array of strings
object (ExternalReferences)

Identifiers for this entity in connected external systems. Each key is the system identifier (sap_po, sap_asset_master, etc.); each value is the identifier in that system.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/locations

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/locations

Transition location lifecycle state

Transitions a location to a new lifecycle state. Valid transitions:

  • planned → active, archived
  • active → under_renovation, decommissioned
  • under_renovation → active, decommissioned
  • decommissioned → archived

Invalid transitions are rejected with 400.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
path Parameters
id
required
string
Request Body schema: application/json
required
to_state
required
string (LocationLifecycleState)
Enum: "planned" "active" "under_renovation" "decommissioned" "archived"

The current lifecycle state of the location.

  • planned — Declared but not yet operational
  • active — Operational; assets and requests can be associated
  • under_renovation — Temporarily not operational
  • decommissioned — No longer operational; existing references preserved
  • archived — Soft-deleted; preserved for historical records
reason
string <= 500 characters

Reason for the transition.

notes
string <= 2000 characters

Additional context for the audit log.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/locations/{id}/transition

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/locations/{id}/transition

Assets

Operations on the assets domain — everything the tenant owns or is responsible for that has identity, lifecycle, and a need to be tracked.

Assets have unique tags, categorisation, current location, custodianship, lifecycle states (procured through disposed), financial properties, and complete history.

See PRD section 8 for the full domain specification.

List assets

Returns a paginated list of assets. Supports filtering by category, location, lifecycle state, custodian, and tags.

For free-text search across asset names, tags, and characteristics, use POST /assets/search.

OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
query Parameters
category_id
string
location_id
string
lifecycle_state
Array of strings (AssetLifecycleState)
Items Enum: "procured" "received" "tagged" "deployed" "in_maintenance" "in_transit" "idle" "lost" "retired" "disposed"
Example: lifecycle_state=deployed
custodian_id
string
tag_pattern
string

Wildcard pattern to match against asset tags (e.g. NRS-HQ-*).

updated_after
string <date-time>
limit
integer [ 1 .. 200 ]

cursor
string

Create asset

Creates a new asset. If tag is omitted, Cadra generates the next available tag per the configured tag schema.

Assets are created in procured state by default if created from procurement context, or in tagged state for manual creation with a tag.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
header Parameters
Idempotency-Key
string
Request Body schema: application/json
required
tag
string (Tag) <= 64 characters ^[A-Z0-9-]+$

Optional explicit tag. If omitted, Cadra generates the next available tag per the configured tag schema for this category and location.

category_id
required
string (Identifier) ^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$

Cadra entity identifier. Format: <prefix>_<26-char-ULID> where prefix is the entity type (e.g. loc for locations, ast for assets, req for requests).

name
required
string <= 255 characters
description
string <= 2000 characters
serial_number
string <= 128 characters
manufacturer
string <= 128 characters
model
string <= 128 characters
current_location_id
required
string (Identifier) ^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$

Cadra entity identifier. Format: <prefix>_<26-char-ULID> where prefix is the entity type (e.g. loc for locations, ast for assets, req for requests).

current_custodian_id
string or null
acquired_at
string <date>
object (Money)
depreciation_method
string (DepreciationMethod)
Enum: "straight_line" "declining_balance" "none" "erp_managed"

The depreciation method for this asset.

  • straight_line — Cadra computes straight-line depreciation
  • declining_balance — Cadra computes declining-balance depreciation
  • none — Asset does not depreciate
  • erp_managed — Depreciation managed by external ERP; current_book_value synced from ERP
useful_life_months
integer
object
tags
Array of strings
parent_asset_id
string or null
object (ExternalReferences)

Identifiers for this entity in connected external systems. Each key is the system identifier (sap_po, sap_asset_master, etc.); each value is the identifier in that system.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/assets

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/assets

Transition asset lifecycle state

Transitions an asset to a new lifecycle state. The state machine enforces permitted transitions:

  • procured → received
  • received → tagged
  • tagged → deployed, idle
  • deployed → in_maintenance, in_transit, idle, lost, retired
  • in_maintenance → deployed, retired
  • in_transit → deployed, idle, lost
  • idle → deployed, retired, in_transit
  • lost → deployed (recovery), retired (write-off)
  • retired → disposed (requires approval and documentation; use /assets/{id}/dispose)

For disposal specifically, use the /dispose endpoint which handles the approval and documentation requirements.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
path Parameters
id
required
string
Request Body schema: application/json
required
to_state
required
string (AssetLifecycleState)
Enum: "procured" "received" "tagged" "deployed" "in_maintenance" "in_transit" "idle" "lost" "retired" "disposed"

The current lifecycle state of the asset.

  • procured — Procurement order exists; goods not yet received
  • received — Goods received, awaiting tagging and configuration
  • tagged — Tag applied, asset registered but not yet deployed
  • deployed — Asset is in active operational use
  • in_maintenance — Asset temporarily withdrawn for service
  • in_transit — Asset is being moved between locations
  • idle — Asset is registered but not in active use
  • lost — Asset cannot be located; under investigation
  • retired — Asset is no longer in active use; awaiting final disposal
  • disposed — Asset has been formally disposed; record preserved for audit

Permitted transitions are defined and enforced by the platform. See the API endpoint /assets/{id}/transition for performing transitions.

reason_code
string
Enum: "fault_reported" "scheduled_service" "relocation" "staff_reassignment" "end_of_life" "damaged_beyond_repair" "stolen" "found_after_lost" "other"

Structured reason code for the transition. Tenants can extend the reason code set.

notes
string <= 2000 characters

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/assets/{id}/transition

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/assets/{id}/transition

Move asset to a new location

Records a movement event and updates the asset's current_location_id. The asset's tag does not change — tag immutability is preserved regardless of moves.

For multi-leg transit, set is_multi_leg: true. The asset enters in_transit state until subsequent legs complete the move.

OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
path Parameters
id
required
string
Request Body schema: application/json
required
to_location_id
required
string (Identifier) ^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$

Cadra entity identifier. Format: <prefix>_<26-char-ULID> where prefix is the entity type (e.g. loc for locations, ast for assets, req for requests).

reason_code
string
notes
string <= 2000 characters
is_multi_leg
boolean
Default: false

If true, asset enters in_transit state until subsequent legs complete the move.

expected_arrival_at
string <date-time> (Timestamp)

ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

Dispose of asset

Initiates the disposal workflow. Disposal requires:

  1. An approval workflow (configurable per tenant; default required)
  2. At least one supporting document attached

On approval and documentation, the asset transitions to disposed. The full record (including history) is preserved for audit.

If the asset is currently in deployed state, disposal transitions it to retired first, then to disposed. Direct transitions from deployed to disposed are not permitted.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
path Parameters
id
required
string
Request Body schema: application/json
required
disposal_method
required
string
Enum: "sale" "scrap" "transfer_to_other_organisation" "destruction" "donation"
object (Money)

Required when disposal_method is sale.

recipient
string <= 255 characters

Buyer (for sale), recipient organisation (for transfer/donation), or scrap merchant.

documentation_refs
Array of strings <uri> [ items <uri > ]

References to supporting documents (sale receipts, scrap certificates, transfer letters).

notes
string <= 5000 characters
supporting_documents
required
Array of strings (Identifier) non-empty [ items^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$ ]

Document IDs of attached supporting documents. At least one is required.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/assets/{id}/dispose

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/assets/{id}/dispose

Service Requests

Operations on the service requests domain — every event in the operational life of an asset or location that needs attention.

Requests have type, status, priority, assignee, SLA, comment threads, and approval workflows. Requests are linked to the assets and locations they concern.

See PRD section 9 for the full domain specification.

List service requests

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
query Parameters
type_id
string
status
Array of strings (RequestStatus)
Items Enum: "draft" "submitted" "triaged" "assigned" "in_progress" "awaiting_requester" "awaiting_approval" "awaiting_parts" "awaiting_third_party" "resolved" "closed" "cancelled" "reopened"
Example: status=in_progress
priority
Array of strings (RequestPriority)
Items Enum: "low" "normal" "high" "critical"
Example: priority=normal
assignee_id
string

string
requester_id
string

string

string

channel
string (Channel)
Enum: "portal" "api" "email" "whatsapp" "sms" "mobile" "walk_in"

Create service request

Creates a new service request. The request type must exist; its routing rules and SLA defaults are applied automatically.

For requests raised through non-API channels (email, WhatsApp), the ingestion service creates requests using this endpoint internally.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
header Parameters
Idempotency-Key
string
Request Body schema: application/json
required
type_id
required
string (Identifier) ^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$

Cadra entity identifier. Format: <prefix>_<26-char-ULID> where prefix is the entity type (e.g. loc for locations, ast for assets, req for requests).

priority
string (RequestPriority)
Enum: "low" "normal" "high" "critical"
subject
required
string <= 255 characters
description
string <= 10000 characters
requester_id
required
string (Identifier) ^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$

Cadra entity identifier. Format: <prefix>_<26-char-ULID> where prefix is the entity type (e.g. loc for locations, ast for assets, req for requests).

requester_channel
string (Channel)
Enum: "portal" "api" "email" "whatsapp" "sms" "mobile" "walk_in"

The channel through which the request was raised.

subject_asset_id
string or null
subject_location_id
string or null
tags
Array of strings
object
object (ExternalReferences)

Identifiers for this entity in connected external systems. Each key is the system identifier (sap_po, sap_asset_master, etc.); each value is the identifier in that system.

initial_attachments
Array of strings (Identifier) [ items^[a-z]{2,6}_[A-Z0-9]{26}$ ]

Document IDs to attach at creation.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/requests

Create webhook subscription

Creates a new webhook subscription. Cadra will deliver matching events to the configured target URL.

The signing secret (if provided) is never returned via API after creation. Store it securely on subscriber's side.

Authorizations:
OAuth2ClientCredentialsBearerToken
Request Body schema: application/json
required
name
string
description
string <= 1000 characters
target_url
required
string <uri>
event_types
required
Array of strings non-empty
authentication_mode
required
string
Enum: "hmac_sha256" "mtls" "bearer_token" "none"
signing_secret
string >= 32 characters

Required when authentication_mode is hmac_sha256. Provide your secret here; Cadra will use it for signing but never return it via API. Rotate periodically.

bearer_token
string

Required when authentication_mode is bearer_token.

object
object

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions

Health

Service health and operational status endpoints.

Service liveness check

Returns 200 if the API service is running. Does not check downstream dependencies (database, Redis, Keycloak).

Use this for basic uptime monitoring; use /health/ready for dependency-aware readiness.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/health

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/health

  • 200
Content type
application/json
{
  • "status": "ok",
  • "version": "1.0.0",
  • "timestamp": "2019-08-24T14:15:22Z"
}

Service readiness check

Returns 200 if the API and its critical dependencies are operational. Returns 503 if any critical dependency is unavailable.

Critical dependencies: PostgreSQL primary, Redis, Keycloak.

Responses

Production (Cadra Enterprise / Standard)

https://{tenant}.cadra.ng/api/v1/health/ready

Staging (for pre-production integration testing)

https://{tenant}.staging.cadra.ng/api/v1/health/ready

  • 503
Content type
application/json

  • "status": "ready",
  • "dependencies": {
    • "database": "healthy",
    • "cache": "healthy",
    • "identity": "healthy"
    }
}

Administration

Platform administration operations.

Most administration is performed via the admin UI; these endpoints support automation and integration with operational tooling.
